heusner1637.cite: Waldispühl, M. & Kopal, N. 2024. Decipherment of a German encrypted letter sent from Sigismund Heusner von Wandersleben to Axel Oxenstierna in 1637. HistoCrypt 2024 Proceedings, 249-253. https://doi.org/10.58009/aere-perennius0116

R4332.note: Date correction: the letter closes 'CASSEL den 15. May 1637', so the date is 15 May 1637, not 15 March. Key re-checked on an independent transcription of letter page 2 (reproduces the published plaintext). Record R3816 carries the same three scans (identical MD5; its P2/P3 = this record's P3/P2): the two records are one letter. Open: the three-digit codes (147-808); 747 occurs in the plaintext but is missing from the key file.

R3816.note: Duplicate of R4332: the three images are byte-identical to R4332's (P1 = R4332 P1, P2 = R4332 P3, P3 = R4332 P2). The letter, Heusner von Wandersleben to Oxenstierna, Kassel 15 May 1637, was deciphered by Waldispühl & Kopal (HistoCrypt 2024); key and plaintext are on R4332. Only the three-digit codes remain open.

R118.note: Not deciphered on the page. The Italian note beneath the figures ('Il Nuntio ha trattato col Sig.r Perez tutto quello che V.S. Ill.ma scrive con la cifra di 19 di sett.re ...') is a clear message, not the decipherment: tested as a crib against the first two lines it fits no better than shuffled controls (43 distinct tokens for 60 letters vs 47-51). The cipher (389 digits, some dotted, plus a barred 4) remains unread; no key found. The note dates the letter to autumn 1576 or 1577 (Rome's cipher of 19 September), not 9 Jan 1576.

R117.note: Not a cipher. The two pages (ff. 245-246) are a clear Spanish memorial, 'Copia del Memorial dado por parte del obispo de Pamplona', on the fruits of the see during the vacancy after Diego Ramírez (d. 27 Jan 1573) until Antonio Manrique's bulls (1575). The only figures are ducat sums in Roman numerals with the thousands sign (e.g. 'xbnUdn L-ix'), repeated in the margin; there is no ciphertext.

R2234.note: Read with the key R2235 (five alphabets D,G,L,N,R): the section capital sets the first line's alphabet, then one alphabet per line in the cycle D-G-L-N-R. Not homophonic.

The letter was deciphered by Cecil at the time (Bain, CSP Scotland I 501: 'a few words in cipher, deciphered by Cecill'); the decipherment is on the original, TNA SP 52/1. The lower half of the page is Sturmius's 1562 key (R9257).
